blocks.text: Re: Engagement for corporate positioning services
Dear Mary:

Thank you for the time you and your colleagues have spent with us in recent weeks. We are pleased to confirm the terms on which Ashcombe Advisory Partners LLC ("Ashcombe") will advise {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} (the "Company") on its corporate positioning. This letter records the approach we discussed, and if any part of it differs from your understanding, we would ask you to tell us before signing so that we can put it right.
The assignment

Our task is to help the Company describe itself clearly and consistently to the audiences on which its next stage depends: the investment community, customers, employees, and the press. Together with you, we will develop a positioning platform that the Company's leadership can adopt as its own, along with the core materials needed to put that platform to use.
Subject to the Company's review and approval at each stage, we expect the work to comprise the following:

items: a review of how the Company presents itself today, drawing on its existing materials, its recent coverage, and confidential conversations with members of its leadership team;
a positioning statement and a supporting message framework, developed with the Company and refined through successive rounds of review;
a standard company description, together with core talking points for executives and designated spokespeople; and
recommendations on introducing the new positioning across the Company's website, press materials, and investor communications, including the order in which those changes should be made.

blocks.text: Services outside this description, such as support for a specific announcement or for an unforeseen reputational matter, are not included. We would be glad to discuss any such work separately, and we will not begin it without your written agreement.
How we will work together

We will work principally through you as the Company's point of contact, and we will confirm decisions and approvals in writing as the engagement proceeds. Drafts will reach you by email with a clear note of what we need from you and by when, so that review on your side remains manageable alongside your other responsibilities.

No statement or material will be released on the Company's behalf without its express approval. The Company retains final authority over all content, and we will treat every draft as confidential until it has been approved for use.
What we will need from the Company

The quality of this work depends on access. We will ask the Company to make members of its leadership team available for interviews and reviews, to provide its existing materials and relevant background promptly, and to inform us of any development that bears on how it should describe itself.
Who will be working with you

As Managing Partner, I will have overall responsibility for the engagement and will review the positioning work at each significant stage. Daniel Valenzuela, an Advisor with the firm, will lead the work day to day and will be your principal contact for scheduling, drafts, and approvals.

Michelle Rose, a Communications Associate, will support our review of the Company's materials and coverage, and she will maintain the media and stakeholder lists on which the later stages of the work rely. Should we need to draw on other members of the firm for particular tasks, we will let you know in advance.
Fees and payment

Our fee for the services described in this letter is a fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2017-001.fee}}. The fee covers the full scope set out above and will change only if we agree with you in writing to change that scope.

We will invoice the fee in installments over the course of the engagement, and each invoice is payable within thirty days of receipt. Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses, such as printing, courier, and media monitoring services, will be billed at cost and incurred only with your prior approval.
Term and termination

The engagement will commence on {{fact:f:E-2017-001.start}}, and we anticipate that the work described above will take approximately five months to complete. Either party may terminate the engagement at any time by written notice to the other.

If the engagement ends before the work is finished, the Company will pay a proportionate share of the fee for services performed, together with approved expenses incurred, through the date of termination. We will deliver to you all work in progress, and the provisions of this letter on confidentiality and limitation of liability will continue to apply.
Confidentiality

We will hold in confidence all non-public information the Company shares with us, use it only for the purposes of this engagement, and disclose it only to those members of our staff who require it for the work. Because the engagement may give us access to material non-public information, each member of our team is bound by the firm's policy on securities trading and disclosure. We advise other companies, some of which may operate in related fields, and we will not use the Company's confidential information in that work.

These obligations do not extend to information that is or becomes public through no fault of ours, or that we are required by law to disclose. Where the law permits, we will notify you promptly before any such disclosure is made.
Limitation of liability

The Company is responsible for the accuracy and completeness of the information it provides to us and for its decisions about what it releases publicly. We will perform our services with the care and skill customary in our profession; we cannot, however, guarantee any particular coverage, market response, or other outcome.

Our aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this engagement will not exceed the fees actually paid to us under this letter. Neither party will be liable to the other for indirect, incidental, or consequential damages.
Governing law

This letter, and any dispute arising from the engagement, is governed by the laws of the state under which Ashcombe Advisory Partners LLC is organized, without regard to that state's conflict-of-laws rules. It constitutes the entire agreement between us on the matters it addresses and may be amended only in a writing signed by both parties.
Your acceptance

We very much look forward to working with you and your colleagues. If these terms are acceptable, please sign where indicated below and return a copy to me, after which Daniel Valenzuela will contact you to arrange our first working session.
Sincerely,
Accepted and agreed on behalf of {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} by its authorized representative:
Memorandum

To: Julie Hill; Christopher Walton; Michelle Rose; Lisa Flores; Pamela Rojas
From: Daniel Valenzuela
Re: Corporate positioning for {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}: kickoff and work plan
What the company needs from us

The corporate positioning engagement for {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} opened on {{fact:f:E-2017-001.start}}. The company needs one clear account of what it does and why that matters, written so that it holds up with investors, customers, employees, and reporters, and adopted by its leadership as its own. By the end of the engagement we owe the company three things: an approved positioning platform, the core materials that carry it, and a plan for putting it into use.

Mary Frank, Director of Operations, is our contact at the company. She arranges our access to the leadership team and approves drafts on the company's behalf, and nothing we write goes to anyone else there until she has seen it.
The work, in order
The work runs in four parts, taken roughly in this sequence, with the media and stakeholder lists kept current throughout:

items: Part 1, listening and audit. Collect the company's current materials (website copy, press releases, investor presentations, recruiting pages) and its recent coverage, and hold confidential interviews with members of the leadership team. Output: a findings memo for Mary Frank.
Part 2, positioning platform. Draft the positioning statement and the message framework beneath it, then take both through review with the company until they are approved.
Part 3, core materials. Turn the approved platform into a standard company description, talking points for executives, and a question and answer document for spokespeople.
Part 4, rollout plan. Recommend the order in which the new language reaches the website, press materials, and investor communications, and identify what has to change first.

Throughout, lists. Keep the company's media list current, with notes on which reporters have covered it and how each prefers to be approached, and keep a matching list of the investors and partners the rollout has to reach.

blocks.text: Who does what

rows: Overall responsibility. Reviews the findings memo, the platform, and the core materials before each goes to the client.
Day-to-day lead and client contact. Runs the interviews and drafts the platform.
Edits the platform and core materials for how they will read to a reporter. Last edit before Julie Hill's review.
Pulls the materials and coverage for the audit. Owns the media and stakeholder lists. Drafting support on the core materials.
Engagement paperwork, billing, and the calendar of client sessions.
Engagement folder and filing. Room bookings and couriers for client sessions.

blocks.text: Before the first interviews
1. Lisa Flores has the countersigned engagement letter on file. Lisa, please open the billing record and send the installment schedule to Mary Frank.

2. Pamela Rojas will set up the engagement folder on the shared drive. Every draft lives there with its version number in the file name, and nothing circulates as an attachment unless a copy is in the folder.
3. Michelle Rose will pull the company's current materials and recent coverage into the folder, so the audit starts from one set of documents.
4. I will send Mary Frank a proposed interview list and ask her to schedule the sessions on the company's side. Christopher Walton and Julie Hill, I would like each of you to sit in on at least one.
5. When the interviews are finished, I will draft the findings memo and circulate it here before anything goes to the client.
The interview list is the first item that has to move. Please send me any names you think belong on it by midweek, and I will send the list to Mary Frank as soon as I have them.
Dear Mary,

I am starting this thread for status on the {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} positioning work, so that updates, questions, and approvals stay in one place. The kickoff memo is attached for reference; it sets out the work plan and the people on our side.

Where things stand: the audit is well under way. We have been through the materials your team sent and the company's recent coverage, and we have now held most of the leadership interviews. The findings memo will follow once the remaining interviews are done, and it will set out what we heard, where the interviews and the current materials agree, and where they do not.

Three items from your side would help us finish this part of the work:
1. Times for the interviews that are still open.
2. The most recent investor presentation, if it differs from the version on the website.
3. The names of anyone besides you who should receive the findings memo.
The open interview times set the pace for everything after them, so if you can send those first, I will build the rest of the schedule around them.
Regards
Mary,

One addition to Daniel's list, if I may. When you send the investor presentation, please include any questions that came up repeatedly in recent investor meetings, with a note of how your team answered them.

Questions of that kind are usually the clearest evidence of where the current description of the company leaves investors uncertain. We would like the findings to take them into account before any positioning language is drafted for {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}.
A short, informal list is entirely sufficient.

Thanks,
JH
Dear Mary,
Thank you for the call this morning. To confirm in writing what we agreed, including Julie's request:

1. You will send the investor presentation together with the recurring questions from recent investor meetings. A rough list is fine.
2. You will book the remaining leadership interviews and send me the times.
3. The findings memo goes to you alone first, and you will decide who else at {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} sees it.
I will hold the findings memo until the investor questions are in, so that it reflects them. When your interview times arrive, I will confirm each one in writing the same day.
Regards
Mary,

Thank you for sending the presentation and the investor questions so promptly. Both are helpful, and the questions in particular give us a clear sense of what investors would like explained more fully.

Daniel's summary of your call matches my understanding, and I have nothing to add to it. We will work the questions into the findings memo, which will come to you before any positioning language is drafted for {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}.

Thanks,
JH
